clue.text: Police call for attention vigorously like this

parts.note: the Old Bill, or just the Bill, is British slang for the police
yo is a shout used to get someone's attention

explanation.surface: An officer shouts for attention in an energetic fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the idiom 'like billy-o', meaning vigorously; the clue's 'like this' supplies the 'like'.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom 'like billy-o' means with great energy, so the word follows 'like' to mean vigorously.

clue.text: A recording for rectification?

indicators.note: rectifying means putting right, so the letters of the clue's first two words are put into a new, corrected order

explanation.surface: Someone wants a tape so that errors can be put right.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of A RECORDING gives a list of corrections, which is exactly what the whole clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrigenda are errors listed for correction in a printed book, so a reshuffle made for rectification fits the plural noun.

clue.text: Group on island can stop

parts.note: a pack is a group, as of wolves or cards
I is the standard abbreviation for island on maps
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A band of people settles on an island and puts a stop to things.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack it in is a British idiom meaning to give up or stop doing something.

clue.text: Still getting interference

definitions.meaning: crackling noise disrupting a broadcast signal

explanation.surface: Staying motionless while being disturbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means unmoving, and as a noun it is the crackling noise that interferes with radio reception.

clue.text: Rolling Stone always provided work for him

definitions.text: Rolling Stone always provided work for him

parts.words: Rolling Stone always provided work for him
parts.note: not the rock band but a figure from Greek myth condemned to push a boulder uphill forever, only to watch it roll down again

explanation.surface: A member of a famous rock band kept someone permanently employed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stone' wants to be Mick Jagger's band; read literally, it is the boulder of the mythical king punished in the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this king was sentenced to roll a stone up a hill for eternity as punishment.

clue.text: Old man, having retired, has little desire for food

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for the father is turned round

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
petite means small or little

explanation.surface: A pensioner father has lost much of his interest in eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' is a common British way to say father, and 'having retired' signals the turnaround, not a pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is the natural wish to eat, a direct synonym for a desire for food.

clue.text: Gift for fellow getting central heating working

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

indicators.note: central asks for the middle letters of the word that follows it

parts.note: on means operating or working, as a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: A present for a college fellow: getting his central heating going again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' takes ATI, the middle three letters of heATIng.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is something given freely, such as money to a charity, so it is a gift.

clue.text: Flower not wholly Hibernian

indicators.note: not wholly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland, so Hibernian means Irish

explanation.surface: A bloom that is only partly from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not wholly' drops the last letter, H, from IRISH.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a garden plant with showy blooms, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Cuckoo sent home for a lark?

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

explanation.surface: A cuckoo is dispatched to someone else's home just for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'for a lark' as 'for fun'; here a lark is the bird, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is where a bird such as a lark lives, so it is a bird's home.

clue.text: Provision in a flexible manner

definitions.meaning: an adverb of supple, meaning pliantly

explanation.surface: A store of goods handled with flexibility.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply is a provision of goods, and supply is also an old adverb from supple meaning pliantly.

clue.text: Attempts to recruit eastern kings as science fiction fans

indicators.note: recruiting means taking people in, so one word holds the others inside it

parts.note: tries are attempts
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Efforts to sign up monarchs from the east as followers of space dramas.
explanation.definitionFit: Trekkies are devoted followers of the Star Trek series, a famous type of science fiction fan.

clue.text: Cherub on stairs forced to flee

parts.note: a putto is a figure of a chubby winged child in Renaissance art
a flight is a set of stairs

explanation.surface: A little angel sitting on a staircase is made to run away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like fleeing, but here it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting someone to flight means making an enemy run away, so it fits forced to flee in the past tense.

clue.text: Survivors getting a large amount of money in old marks?

parts.note: livers, taken literally, are those who live on, survivors
pots of money is an idiom for a great deal of it

explanation.surface: Those who come through it receive a fortune in obsolete German currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old marks' suggests former Deutschmarks; in fact it means the blemishes of old age.
explanation.definitionFit: Liver spots are brown patches on the skin that come with age, so they are marks of the old.

clue.text: Intended to cure soldiers getting laid up

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Troops confined to bed are being treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid up' suggests bedridden soldiers; in a down clue, 'up' turns the word around.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedial means meant to set something right, from remedy, so it describes treatment designed to heal.

clue.text: Long poem by Keats done in my style

indicators.note: putting the letters in a new style means rearranging the three words before it

explanation.surface: Someone writes a long Keats poem imitating their own manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's long narrative poem of 1818 tells of the shepherd loved by the moon goddess and opens 'A thing of beauty is a joy for ever'.

clue.text: Hoffman lacks capital — over 50% is provided by British actor

indicators.note: lacking its capital means losing its first letter

parts.note: Dustin Hoffman is the American film actor

indicators.note: fifty per cent means half of the following word, its first half

explanation.surface: An American star falls short on finance, so a British actor puts up more than half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks capital' removes D from DUSTIN; '50%' takes OV, the first half of over.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Ustinov was a British actor, writer and raconteur, an Oscar winner for Spartacus.

clue.text: No friend rings in to provide name

indicators.note: rings means surrounds, so one word encircles the other

parts.note: mate is British slang for friend

explanation.surface: A friend who won't phone to give a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' suggests telephoning, but here it means encircles; 'to provide' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate is to put a person forward by name, so as verbs the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Grandma piercing cloth

parts.note: nan is a British informal word for grandmother
keen means sharp or piercing, as a keen wind

explanation.surface: Grandmother pushes a needle through some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton fabric originally made in Nanjing, so it is a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Time in Memory Lane, recollecting deadly foe?

indicators.note: in places one letter within the scrambled phrase
re-collecting means gathering again, so the letters of the phrase are gathered into a new order

explanation.surface: Spending time on a nostalgic trip, remembering an old enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollecting' turns MEMORY LANE into MORALENEMY, and 'in' puts T inside it after MOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortal enemy is a bitter, lifelong foe, and deadly is the literal sense of mortal.

clue.text: Side one's duplicated

definitions.meaning: a team of ... players, as in football or cricket

explanation.surface: A team in which one player is copied.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has eleven players, and writing the figure one twice gives 11.

clue.text: Work with duck and cat mostly

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: puss is a familiar name for a cat

explanation.surface: Most of a job done involving a duck and a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the final S from PUSS.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a work, especially a numbered musical composition.

clue.text: The language of poetry needing no introduction

indicators.note: with no introduction means without its first letter

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Poetic diction that speaks for itself and needs no preamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no introduction' takes V off the front of VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Unloved clergyman is eating soft veg?

indicators.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, so losing love means dropping an O

parts.note: a parson is a parish clergyman

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: A lonely vicar dines on mushy vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unloved' uses the tennis convention of love as zero, and 'eating' signals one piece swallowing another.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsnips are pale root vegetables; the question mark admits 'veg' is plural and informal.

clue.text: Lorenzo the Magnificent was one by the sea here in France

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
ici is French for here

explanation.surface: A Renaissance ruler was a man of the French seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorenzo the Magnificent ruled Florence as head of the powerful Medici banking family.

clue.text: Almost eat items containing soapstone

indicators.note: containing means the answer sits inside the run of words before it

explanation.surface: Eating nearly all of some items containing soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Steatite is the mineral talc in massive form, the soft rock otherwise called soapstone.

clue.text: Archer gets nothing new from shop

parts.note: William Tell is the legendary Swiss archer who shot an apple from his son's head
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A bowman receives nothing fresh from the store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' looks like a store; it is the British slang verb meaning to inform on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell on someone and to shop them both mean to report them to the authorities.
